title: SYSK Selects: How Sleepwalking Works
summary: Selects rerun of the Stuff You Should Know episode on sleepwalking (somnambulism). The hosts open with the 1845 Maria Ann Bickford murder case in Weymouth, Massachusetts, in which Albert Terrell claimed sleepwalking and was acquitted, then cover the official definition of sleepwalking (DSM-IV), when it occurs in non-REM deep sleep, why it is hard to wake someone, the myth about waking sleepwalkers, prevalence and family/twin links, possible causes (sleep deprivation, stress, epilepsy association, hormones, brainstem theories), sleepwalking criminal cases, other parasomnias such as sleep sex and sleep eating linked to Ambien (zolpidem), sleep emailing, sleepwalking injuries, REM sleep behavior disorder, and personal anecdotes. The episode ends with a listener mail story about a grandmother who grew marijuana plants.

segments.title: Selects intro and 1845 Weymouth murder case
segments.summary: Josh introduces the Selects episode and tells the story of Maria Ann Bickford's murder, with Albert Terrell acquitted on a sleepwalking claim.

segments.title: Definition and timing of sleepwalking
segments.summary: The hosts define sleepwalking (somnambulism) using the DSM-IV criteria and explain that it occurs in deep non-REM sleep, when the body moves but the brain is not dreaming.

segments.title: Waking sleepwalkers and what they do
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why sleepwalkers are hard to wake, the myth that waking them is dangerous, and that episodes usually last under half an hour and rarely recur in a night.

segments.title: Prevalence, family history, and risks
segments.summary: Sleepwalking runs in families, is more common in children and identical twins, affects a small percentage of adults, and can be a symptom of conditions like dementia or Parkinson's; injuries are discussed.

segments.title: Causes and competing theories
segments.summary: Theories include transitions between sleep and wakefulness, sleep deprivation, stress, hormones in children, epilepsy association, and brainstem activity; a buzzer study is described.

segments.title: Sleepwalking criminal cases
segments.summary: The hosts discuss sleepwalking cases in court, including murder and assault convictions and acquittals, and a recent Illinois acquittal.

segments.title: Other parasomnias: sleep sex, sleep eating, sleep emailing, falls
segments.summary: The hosts cover sleep sex, sleep eating linked to Ambien, a sleep-emailing woman, and a fall from a hotel window in Majorca, along with a quicksand incident on Holy Island.

segments.title: Personal anecdotes and REM sleep behavior disorder
segments.summary: Hosts share sleepwalking and sleep-talking stories, including Josh's uncle, and explain that acting out dreams belongs to REM sleep behavior disorder rather than sleepwalking.

segments.title: Listener mail: pot growing grandmother
segments.summary: A listener describes her grandmother growing marijuana plants in her Pennsylvania yard after a frat brother supplied seeds.
